methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $84M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
LuxWall, a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $84M to date, is evaluated against a peer universe of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy) representing the most directly comparable set, alongside a broader comp base of 9 private firms and 1 public comparator (LNZA).

Two valuation methods triangulate LuxWall's value. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $84M total raised proxy, implying $160M. Peer-median analysis across the 3-company set yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. The stage-progression method anchors to capital deployment efficiency; the peer-median reflects market pricing for climate-tech companies at comparable or proximate development stages.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $136M to $1.1B, with a median of $580M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty inherent in the stage and sector: comparable firms show substantial valuation variance ($700M to $3.0B), and LuxWall's specific technology maturity, revenue profile, and capital efficiency relative to named peers remain undefined. The gap between stage-progression and peer medians suggests valuation hinges critically on LuxWall's execution trajectory and defensibility relative to the sampled peer cohort.
